title: The Bridge of the Lower Danube
premise: In the winter of 1916, Petra Okonkwo, a Nigerian-born nurse serving at a field hospital on the Lower Danube, keeps a secret ledger of the wounded soldiers whose names the officers' reports omit. When the season's last bridge crossing closes and an armistice investigation arrives at the hospital, Petra's ledger becomes evidence in a reckoning no one in command wants. As the river freezes and the workshop where the ledger is hidden faces demolition, Petra must finish recording every name before the supply ship sails on the morning tide — the only way the truth leaves the valley. The book ends with the ledger aboard the departing ship, Petra staying behind among the people she has come to belong to, having learned that history happens wherever someone refuses to let names be erased.
about_author: Beatrix Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial-era medical records from the Danube campaigns. She writes historical fiction about the people official histories leave out, and lives near a river she still cannot stop watching.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Petra, working triage in a converted granary hospital, records the name of a dying Serbian conscript that the morning report omits. Her POV establishes her belief that history happens elsewhere, to other people. Emotional beat: quiet defiance disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Frost on the Wire
chapters.summary: Major Aldous Reeve inspects the hospital and praises its 'immaculate anonymity.' Petra observes how paperwork erases men while he watches. His POV briefly shows his own anxieties about a pending inquiry. Beat: unease beneath politeness.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Engineers detonate the ice-choked pontoon spans; the only road out of the valley shuts for the season. Petra realizes she, the wounded, and the truth are all trapped together. Beat: claustrophobia turning into resolve.

chapters.title: Names Without Nations
chapters.summary: Petra tends Ilya, a soldier who claims three nationalities and none, and begins questioning what a name is worth if no state will claim it. Ilya's POV. Beat: tenderness across language barriers.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Arrives
chapters.summary: Captain Verena Hoss, a war-crimes investigator cut off from headquarters by the closed bridge, takes over the granary's back room. She discovers one page of Petra's ledger by accident. Beat: wary alliance between two women who distrust institutions differently.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Hoss reconstructs a massacre at Kladovo from ration records; Petra supplies the missing human column. Their joint work becomes dangerous as Reeve notices the back room's lamp burning late. Beat: purpose hardening into risk.

chapters.title: The Workshop
chapters.summary: Petra hides the growing ledger in a boatwright's workshop by the water, run by old Mirko, who lost two sons to the war and asks no questions. Mirko's POV. Beat: found family forming in exile.

chapters.title: Reeve's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Reeve orders the hospital's records 'standardized,' meaning purged. Petra copies names through the night while fevers spike around her. Beat: exhaustion transfigured into devotion.

chapters.title: Ilya's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilya admits he was part of the unit Hoss is investigating — a witness, not a killer, but complicit enough to hang. He begs Petra to omit him from the ledger. Beat: the ethics of memory tested by mercy.

chapters.title: A Name Withheld
chapters.summary: Petra faces her first blank line. Hoss argues testimony matters more than purity; Mirko says a man is more than his worst winter. Beat: moral crisis at the heart of the book.

chapters.title: The Frozen Crossing
chapters.summary: Deserters attempt to cross the ice at night; several drown within sight of the hospital windows. Petra pulls one survivor ashore against orders. Beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Reeve Learns of the Ledger
chapters.summary: A search of the granary finds nothing, but Reeve suspects and posts guards on the workshop. Hoss realizes her own commission may be recalled before it reports. Beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Mirko's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mirko offers Reeve a forged inventory to buy time, trading his workshop's legitimacy for the ledger's safety. Beat: sacrifice offered quietly, refused thanks.

chapters.title: The Ship on the Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Word comes: a neutral supply ship will take mail and witnesses downriver when the ice breaks — one departure, one chance for the ledger to reach the outside world. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Testimony of the Wounded
chapters.summary: Petra and Hoss spend three days taking statements from men well enough to speak, including Ilya, who chooses to sign his true name after all. Beat: courage contagious; the withheld line finally filled.

chapters.title: Reeve's Counterattack
chapters.summary: Reeve declares the hospital infected with typhus and orders quarantine — a legal fiction to seal the ledger inside. Hoss is confined; Petra is reassigned to the dying ward. Beat: injustice wearing procedure's face.

chapters.title: Breaking Quarantine
chapters.summary: Petra smuggles the ledger out in a coffin during a burial detail, with Mirko driving the cart and the dead soldier's mother keeping watch. Beat: the living conspiring with the dead.

chapters.title: The Workshop Stands or Falls
chapters.summary: Reeve orders the workshop demolished as a 'navigation hazard.' Petra, Mirko, and recovered patients work through the night to move the boat containing the ledger to deep water before the demolition crew arrives. Beat: race against machinery.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Ice
chapters.summary: Reeve catches them at the slipway. Hoss, escaped confinement, invokes her commission and names the massacre aloud before the assembled garrison. Reeve falters — his own omitted names are read back to him. Beat: climax; justice spoken outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: At dawn the ship's boat takes the ledger and Hoss aboard. Ilya chooses to go as witness; Petra chooses to stay. The ship clears the broken ice as the valley watches. Beat: release and loss entwined.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Spring floods carry away the last of the bridge timbers. Petra reopens the hospital under new command, the purge reversed, the record restored. Beat: quiet restoration.

chapters.title: Every Name Read Aloud
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, the townspeople gather in the rebuilt workshop while Petra reads the complete ledger aloud — every name, including Ilya's, now carried in print from the world beyond the river. Beat: belonging achieved; history made here, by them.
